title: DiffuMamba: High-Throughput Diffusion LMs with Mamba Backbone
claim: A backbone built from repeated blocks can swap its costly global-mixing layer for an efficient alternative while keeping the overall architecture unchanged.
layout: 2 panels, bottom-to-top flow, dotted zoom-in lines from block to detail
description: A block diagram of a neural architecture, drawn with pastel rounded boxes and arrows that run bottom to top. The left panel is the full model. Tokens feed an Embedding box, which merges with a Noise Conditioning box and enters a Diffusion Block marked 'N×'. Above it sit Layer Norm, Linear Reshape and Logits. A thick skip line carries Noise Conditioning up to the Linear Reshape box. Dotted lines run from the Diffusion Block to the right panel, which zooms into the block. There, Noise and Input boxes feed an 'Attention/Bi-Mamba' box, then RMS Norm, then an MLP. A residual line with a ⊕ node sits at the top, and a dashed line carries noise to the MLP. Colors mark module types: yellow for data, purple for noise, blue for norms, green for mixers, red for linear and MLP layers.
caption: Schematic diagram of our proposed \dm\ architecture where mixer blocks replaces attention layers with bidirectional Mamba layers. For \dimh\ we have interleaved attention layers after every $N-1$ Mamba layers. Attention provides global token interactions while Mamba enables efficient state space sequence modeling, allowing the hybrid denoiser to capture both long-range dependencies and local temporal dynamics with significantly improved efficiency. In our experiments, we fix $N=5$.
abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive (AR) generation, yet their reliance on Transformer backbones limits inference efficiency due to quadratic attention or KV-cache overhead. We introduce DiffuMamba, a masked diffusion language model built on a bidirectional Mamba backbone that combines the diffusion objective with linear-time sequence modeling, and DiffuMamba-H, a hybrid variant with interleaved attention. Across scales up to 1.3B parameters, our models match Transformer-based diffusion in downstream performance while achieving up to 8.2x and 4.3x higher inference throughput, respectively, on long sequences. We further present a systematic analysis of inference efficiency across modern DLM variants combining asymptotic complexity with empirical measurements. Notably, cache-efficient block diffusion with Mamba mixers emerges as the only strategy that scales linearly with sequence length and achieves the strongest performance across all baselines, suggesting a promising direction for future diffusion-based generation systems.
